subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced final-reply `MEDIA:` lines remain non-delivered with a warning, be extracted when valid and standalone, or be documented as invalid with no runtime diagnostic?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves fenced code examples as text, while the reported user problem is silent attachment loss; extraction changes delivery semantics and warn-only changes diagnostics without changing extraction.

options.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
options.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines visible as text but emit one clear warning at the real outbound delivery boundary when delivery was likely intended.

options.title: Extract fenced standalone tokens
options.body: Treat valid standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting the risk that examples may become deliveries.

options.title: Document as invalid only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs plus prompt guidance to prevent invalid fenced legacy directives.

recommendation.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines visible as text but emit one clear warning at the real outbound delivery boundary when delivery was likely intended.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the live reviewer on the candidate PR and already framed the parser-purity and delivery-boundary warning decision.
